newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.00 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Tuesday were steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, supported by competition among packers for light hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $55.50 to $56.50 at plants, dealers and packer buyers there said.

Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $54.50 to $55.00 in the country and $55.50 to $56.00 at plants, with talk that some packers reportedly paid $57.00 for top quality hogs, Illinois sources said.
Indiana hogs sold $0.50 higher at $55.00 to $55.50 in the country and $56.50 at plants, although $57.00 was possible if demand remains strong and movement light, dealers said.
Ohio hogs sold fully steady in light volume at $54.00 to $54.50 in the country and $55.00 to $55.50 at plants.

The light marketings were tied to a seasonal reduction in hog supplies. Marketings last week were heavy for a short time following the Monday Memorial Day holiday, but quickly faded once hogs held back by the holiday had been sold, they said.
"They're just not there now," one Indiana buyer said.
